# kiwix

**The Kiwix desktop reader for offline Wikipedia and other ZIM books**

- **Version recorded:** 2.4.1
- **Categories:** `references`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/kiwix/kiwix-desktop>

## What it does

A desktop application that opens ZIM files -- offline Wikipedia, WikiMed, Stack Exchange sites and the rest of the Kiwix library -- in tabs, with search and bookmarks, the way a browser opens web pages.

## Why you would want it

It is the easiest way into a book on a laptop: open the file and read. `hammunition reference serve` does the same in any browser and also shows the ICS forms and dictionaries; this is for the operator who wants a reader window rather than a local web page.

## Before it will work

A desktop session, and books: `kiwix-library` installs the ones you choose under /usr/local/share/hammunition/data/kiwix-library/, which you open by file from the reader.

## How it installs

- apt: `kiwix`

## Known problems

It keeps its own library, so books installed by `kiwix-library` are opened once by file and then remembered; it does not read Hammunition's list. Its built-in downloader fetches books without the pin and sha256 check `kiwix-library` applies; prefer the catalog's books. Qt5 WebEngine is a large dependency on a desktop without it.

## Keeping it current

- probe: apt policy
- strategy: apt_upgrade

## Where to get help with the software itself

The Kiwix project's issue tracker on GitHub (https://github.com/kiwix/kiwix-desktop/issues) and https://kiwix.org/.
